synopsis: SOTIF concerns unsafe sensing or decision-making despite no broken parts, including both missed people and nuisance braking for harmless objects [f12007, f12013]. ISO 21448:2022 is a road-vehicle standard outside the scope of heavy off-road machines; the booklet nevertheless borrows its triggering-condition logic for scenarios, requirements and the perception safety case [f2355, f12008, f12015, f15295]. The booklet pairs ISO 19014 for the intervention chain with SOTIF-related perception concepts, but functional safety and fault injection alone cannot establish healthy-system perception performance [f12018, f12021, f1009]. Visibility in dust, snow, fog, glare and darkness remains the hardest uncertainty and the least suited to simulation, so perception robustness must rest on physical and recorded-sensor evidence [f12019, f12020]. The research did not verify the on-road ISO 21448 approach, and Chapter 8's evidence linking braking safety and perception limits is draft, limiting the assurance planners can draw from these references [f5812, f6580].
